brief.headline: Blackstone Agreed to Invest About $535 Million in IIFL Finance for a Stake of Roughly 16% in a Rs 6,414 Crore Capital Raise
bullets: M&A & Buyouts: Funds managed by Blackstone Private Equity will invest Rs 5,000 crore, about $535 million, in Indian non-bank lender IIFL Finance.

Fundraising: Carlyle Group and SEI Investments have launched a private markets fund targeting individual investors, with a minimum investment of $1,000, as alternative asset managers continue expanding their distribution into the wealth management market, according to a report by Bloomberg.
Real Estate: Honda announced it will invest $3 billion to build a new auto plant in Central Ohio, increasing its U.S. auto production capacity to approximately 1.3 million vehicles a year.

AI & Technology: In his latest memo, Howard Marks, Co-Chair of Oaktree and Chair of Brookfield's Investment Solutions Group, revisits the topic of artificial intelligence, describing it as both deeply consequential and highly unpredictable.

M&A & Buyouts: KKR and US energy producer Diamondback Energy have agreed to acquire Five Point Infrastructure's 70% stake in Deep Blue Midland Basin, a water infrastructure business operating in Texas's Permian Basin, in a transaction valued at approximately $2.1bn, according to a report by Reuters.
brief.marketRead: Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits. The S&P 500 stands at 7,520.93 (down 0.4% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 19.5, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.88% (up 2 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.25 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.34%, near long-run norms (down 8 bps on the prior reading).
